content:
As the "Surprise and shine" September event wraps up, Apple today officially released the RC (release candidate) builds of iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, and other operating systems.

RC builds such as iPadOS 27 are available for testing starting today

Apple's major software updates for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other devices are about to roll out.

iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27, tvOS 27, and visionOS 27 will be pushed out to all users next Monday (September 14).

After a full summer of beta testing, Apple today began pushing the RC builds of the above updates to users.

Developers and public beta users can install RC builds such as iPadOS 27 through the "Software Update" page in Settings.

Release candidates (RC) are generally considered the final version of the software and will be released directly to all users. However, if Apple discovers any major issues that need fixing, we may see an RC 2 release very soon.

Apple typically rolls out RC builds of its major software right after its annual iPhone event — a practice that has become standard.

The reason for this is that not all new features are usually announced at WWDC; some are only revealed at the September event. For example, Apple today unveiled several watchOS 27 features at its Apple Watch hardware event that were never mentioned at WWDC in June, and they are now included in the watchOS 27 RC.

Have you spotted any new features in Apple's RC builds? Feel free to tell us in the comments.

For more coverage of Apple's events, visit our dedicated event hub.
